headline: Committee votes on pedestrian, housing and grid policies; review continues tomorrow

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.voteItem: Motion to add back a policy on housing projects presenting to a community association
meeting.summary: Members voted 7–0 on pedestrian-oriented development and on housing projects presenting to community groups, and 5–0 on grid hardening. A roll call on restoring a deleted infrastructure policy ended four ayes, one no, four excused, with no result stated.
meeting.recap: Members agreed to judge repeated policies case by case and mark kept ones with an asterisk.[[0:27:14]] A change tying a tree policy to the urban forest plan passed 6–1 on a roll call.[[0:52:32]] Members voted 7–0 to require pedestrian-oriented new developments, with mixed uses required "to the extent practicable.".[[1:31:10]] The planning director said 34% of Kīhei-Mākena Community Plan actions are complete and 12% have not begun.[[1:39:19]] Members voted 7–0 to encourage housing projects to present to the nearest community association or citizens organization.[[2:02:18]] The chair plans to wait on Section 3 decisions until pending responses come back, which would be next term.[[2:57:53]] Members voted 6–0 to keep "discourage new transient units" and drop a luxury-home workforce housing rule.[[3:26:46]] The chair raised restoring a deleted policy allowing no further development unless needed infrastructure is in place.[[4:29:36]] The roll call on restoring it was four ayes, one no and four excused, with no result stated.[[4:49:03]] Members voted 5–0 to encourage grid hardening so the power grid can withstand severe weather.[[5:03:49]] The chair said members may hold an executive session (a closed-door discussion) for legal advice tomorrow.[[5:15:00]]
decided: The committee voted to add a policy encouraging housing projects to present to the nearest existing community association or citizens organization.
The committee kept "discourage new transient units" and did not adopt a separate rule on workforce housing in luxury developments.
The roll call ended at four ayes, one no and four excused, and the captions do not state whether it passed.
The committee voted to encourage grid hardening, with examples from the advisory committee's draft added.
The committee voted to use the recommended grid language and delete the two policies listed after it.
meeting.next: The chair plans to hold off on decisions about Section 3 until pending responses come back. Committee resources may show drone footage of sites members could not visit.

boards.name: Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

issues.oneLine: The draft plan asks new hotels and hotel expansions to be water neutral "to the extent practicable.".
issues.why: The planning director said a new hotel starts from zero water use, so it could not truly be net zero.
issues.brief: The Planning Commission added the words "to the extent practicable" to the advisory committee's hotel water policy.[[#1]] Planning staff said water neutrality means no net depletion of freshwater resources.[[#2]]

issues.oneLine: Members voted to encourage grid hardening so the electric grid can withstand severe weather.
issues.why: A council member said the Kīhei community spoke strongly about emergency evacuations, citing the Lahaina Fire.
issues.brief: The advisory committee chair said connecting cul-de-sacs matters for people's lives after the fires.[[#1]] A council member said any small storm can close South Kīhei Road, leaving one way in and out.[[#2]]
